messages.subject: sim.cross
parts:
Dear Colleagues,

I need to (i) assign one QTL to each of 5 parameters I have; (ii) them
combine all together in a kind of linear combination; and finally
(iii) look for these QTL in the final linear combination.

I have the same map for all of the 5 parameters. Then I used the
function sim.cross to simulate the QTLs in each of the 5 parameters
(in the positions I have choose). But the problem rises when I try to
combine all together in a "linear combination" because the phenotypic
and genotypic data are generated each time I run the sim.cross.

My question is whether there is any way to "put" a QTL in a given
position keeping unchanged the genotypic data (only changing the
phenotypic data). I mean, using the sim.cross where the map and
genotypic data are fixed.

Thank you in advanced for you comments.
Best regards,
Paulo Canas Rodrigues.

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] sim.cross
parts:
Dear Paulo,

I don't really understand the question, but if you simulate QTL with sim.cross, the QTL genotypes are retained in the cross object as an element "qtlgeno", and so you can use them to simulate new phenotypes with the same set of genotypes.

For example:

data(map10)

x <- sim.cross(map10, type="bc", n.ind=250,
model=rbind(c(1, 50, 1), c(2, 50, 1), c(3, 50, 1), c(4, 50, 1), c(5, 50, 1)))

x$pheno[,2] <- x$qtlgeno %*% rep(1, 5) + rnorm(nind(x))

x <- calc.genoprob(x, step=1)
out <- scanone(x, phe=1:2, method="hk")
plot(out, lod=1:2, col=c("blue", "red"))

See also Sec 2.5 in Broman & Sen, A guide to QTL mapping with R/qtl, http://www.rqtl.org/book

regards,
karl

kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu
